The work's first fully automatic brewing system.

Interesting.

I'm a distiller and before that I was a brewer for a decade or so.

There are a few things I like. First of all, it uses a very small amount of water compared to the normal brewing process. For drought impact states, this is a pretty big deal. I would say that burn through about ten more gallons per batch than this would use. That's hundreds of gallons saved per year. I also like that it's a compact system, and relatively self cleaning. If i was making beer out of my house, I could do it in the kitchen instead of my garage. It's also an electrical system, making it far better than most systems where we're using propane to heat. Finally, this is a much easier way to brew. You're not transferring the wort from a mash tun to a boiling vessel. You're not using a wort chiller. You're not spending an hour to se up your brew day. That's pretty appealing.

Now the bad parts. First off is the price. For a few hundred dollars I can take you down to Home Depot and get you set up with a system. This is two grand. There's plenty of other things I would buy with that cash. Chugger pumps. Refrigeration system. More kegs. Plenty of things. Next, I'm not too enthused about fermenting inside a keg. For one thing, you can't see what's happening with the yeast. Until you know the yeast inside and out, you're going to need to use your eyeballs to se when fermentation has stalled. There's also the issue that once you're done, you're still going to need yet another keg to transfer the beer into. Those airlocks used won't last for long. It won't be cheap, I imagine, to get replacements.

Worst of all, I don't think that this system will help teach you anything about brewing. The reason you make your own beer is to learn the art and skills of it. If you just want to drink good beer, go down to the store. If you want to learn how to brew, than this won't teach you that much. The process is important. By staring with cobbled together equipment, you upgrade as your skills increase. You learn what's happening in the boil. You learn what the ingredients do.

If you have lots of money burning a hole in your pocket, and you just want to say "this is beer I made", then why the hell not. I have a feeling this will make some good stuff.
